visual_source_files.evidence: GitHub README title/authors/ICLR 2026 Oral match the PDF and the README says code will be released soon; gh recursive tree contains no plot, table, TeX, notebook, data or rendered visual source.

source_acquisition.search_note: PDF explicit GitHub URL → OpenReview/reading metadata → source inventory candidate → gh repository metadata and recursive tree. The public repository is real and title-matched but contains only README.md; no local visual source directory exists. All visual judgments therefore use the PDF as fact source and 200 dpi rendered observations; no source file is promoted to plot_script, table_generator, paper_tex or rendered_asset.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Pastel role colors encode method stages and architecture components; saturated red/blue overlays encode unstable and re-optimized route edges; green/blue/mustard line families identify backbone solvers. Text, line style, panel order and shapes provide partial redundancy, but the palette is not fully grayscale-safe.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: PDF text, rules, axes, architecture and flow lines are predominantly vector; result curves and several route-case panels are mixed; Figure 8, Figure 9 and Figure 12 include rasterized visual panels. pdffonts and pdfimages confirm mixed embedded objects, while no editable author source is public.
paper_style.style_consistency: Caption placement and Figure/Table numbering are stable. Route-edge red/blue semantics persist across the appendix and SYN/NAR/AR order recurs. Font families, small-label sizes and pastel-versus-saturated palettes vary between imported method diagrams, quantitative plots and raster route panels.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Percentage of re-optimized edges during iterative search using LKH-3 on 100 CVRP instances. Most edges remain unchanged, suggesting redundant calculations.

color.semantic_mapping: Green and blue identify CVRP2k/CVRP3k; curve position encodes re-optimized-edge percentage and pale ribbons surround the curves.

figures.data_and_statistics: A 100-instance CVRP aggregation is shown as two declining curves. The text reports an initial fraction near 30% that falls to single digits; the PDF does not state the exact per-step aggregation, the number of instances contributing to each point beyond the 100-instance pool, or what the translucent ribbons mean. They are therefore recorded as a visible but statistically undefined band, not as a confidence interval.
figures.evidence_relation: The percentage motivates the claim that iterative LKH-3 repeatedly recomputes mostly stable edges. It supports the mechanism premise for FSTA, but does not itself establish an end-to-end speedup.
design_strengths: A single descending mechanism curve makes the motivation immediately legible.
The caption states the 100-instance denominator and the interpretation of unchanged edges.
Color, position and legend text provide enough redundancy to follow the two scales.
design_weaknesses: The ribbon semantics are absent, so it is unsafe to read them as uncertainty.
Search-step count and exact aggregation are not exposed, and the small single-column plot limits label readability.
No per-instance spread or failure count is supplied.
figures.reusable_pattern: Quantify structural change across solver iterations first, then connect the stable remainder to the later aggregation diagram; define any ribbon in the caption.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: The overview of our FSTA decomposition framework (top) and the three proposed L2Seg models (bottom). L2Seg-SYN employs a four-step synergized approach: (1) problem decomposition into subproblems, (2) unstable nodes detection globally via NAR decoding, (3) clustering of NAR-predicted nodes to localize unstable regions and select initial target nodes, and (4) refining unstable edge predictions locally via AR decoding starting from these identified initial target nodes.

color.semantic_mapping: Pastel blocks encode FSTA stages and decoder components; green solid, yellow dotted and brown dashed paths encode SYN, NAR and AR. Arrows, labels and node shapes repeat the color semantics.

encodings.x: ordered FSTA stage sequence from solution to recovered solution
encodings.color: FSTA stage blocks and SYN/NAR/AR method paths
encodings.line: solid/dotted/dashed decoder paths and directional arrows
encodings.facet: top framework and bottom three decoder paths
encodings.text: stage labels, method labels and numbered SYN steps

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual algorithm interface only. The top path has five visible operations (detect, group, aggregate, re-optimize, recover); the caption describes the four synergized SYN operations. No sample size, objective, timing or uncertainty statistic is plotted.
figures.evidence_relation: The top-level decomposition operationalizes the stable-edge premise from Figure 1; the bottom paths explain why SYN combines NAR global node detection, K-means localization and AR local refinement. Figure 3 and Figure 4 provide the architecture and label-construction evidence, while Tables 1, 3 and 4 test the resulting variants.
design_strengths: The outer solver loop and inner model paths share one reading direction.
The caption enumerates SYN operations and the visual uses distinct path styles.
Stage blocks, arrows, labels and node shapes provide multimodal method encoding.
design_weaknesses: Many small labels and two semantic layers compete for the same page-width canvas.
The five visible top operations and four captioned SYN steps are not explicitly numbered as a one-to-one mapping.
No quantitative failure or uncertainty channel is present.
figures.reusable_pattern: Place the system-level loop above the model-level paths and number the handoff between them; attach a measurable output to each interface node.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: Architecture of L2Seg: encoder (left), NAR decoder (center), and AR decoder (right). NAR predicts unstable nodes for associated edges. AR uses a two-stage process, where the insertion bridges the deletion stage to accurately detect unstable edges locally, akin to the local search behavior.

color.semantic_mapping: Pink, green and blue component backgrounds identify encoder, NAR and AR; module boxes, node/edge drawings and arrows redundantly identify the tensor/data flow.

encodings.x: encoder to NAR decoder to AR decoder information flow
encodings.y: submodule hierarchy within the three columns
encodings.color: encoder/NAR/AR component backgrounds and state roles
encodings.shape: graph nodes, edge types and rounded module boxes
encodings.line: data-flow arrows and solid/dotted/dashed stage links
encodings.facet: encoder, NAR decoder and AR decoder columns
encodings.text: layer names, equations, state labels and output labels

figures.data_and_statistics: Architecture diagram with no sample-level statistics. It exposes route Transformer, graph encoder/GAT, MLP+Sigmoid NAR output, and AR deletion/insertion state flow; layer symbols are stated in the drawing and their values are provided in Table 10.
figures.evidence_relation: The shared encoder and complementary decoders are the implementation-level realization of Figure 2. Their predicted node/edge behavior is measured by Table 4 and illustrated by Figure 6 and Figure 12; Table 10 supplies the hyperparameters.
design_strengths: Three aligned columns make the encoder/NAR/AR boundary explicit.
Intermediate states such as initial/last/available nodes and deletion/insertion are shown rather than hidden.
Component colors match the method family in Figure 2.
design_weaknesses: The graph input, layer hierarchy, symbols and intermediate states make the diagram dense at single-page scale.
Parameter values and tensor shapes are deferred to Table 10.
The diagram does not show training loss weights or failure boundaries.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a fixed three-column architecture skeleton with a visible probability output and a visible local sequence output, then bind every symbol to a reproduction table.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4: Training data construction for the AR model. Re-optimization reveals deleted edges (blue/green dashed) and inserted edges (red dashed) forming connected components (circles). For each component, depth-first search generates node sequences alternating between deletion and insertion stages, terminated by an end token as the AR model’s training label.

color.semantic_mapping: Red dashed inserted edges, blue/green deleted-edge stages, circles for connected components, and arrows for DFS sequence order.

encodings.x: original difference graph to component example to sequence label
encodings.y: graph construction above and alternating deletion/insertion sequence below
encodings.shape: connected-component circles, graph nodes and End token
encodings.line: dashed edge states and DFS/sequence arrows
encodings.facet: difference graph, component zoom and AR label sequence
encodings.text: stage labels, node ids and End token

figures.data_and_statistics: Training-label construction is shown as a structural example rather than a sample statistic. Re-optimization produces deleted/inserted edge sets, connected components and DFS sequences; no count, threshold or class balance is plotted.
figures.evidence_relation: The lookahead-label process in Figure 4 supplies AR supervision for the architecture in Figure 3. It connects the solver difference to Table 9 training parameters and to the AR/SYN results in Table 1.
design_strengths: The same node identities can be followed from difference graph to sequence.
The caption defines edge colors, component circles and the end token.
The graph-to-sequence transition makes the training interface concrete.
design_weaknesses: The upper graph and lower sequence require careful visual matching in a small column.
No positive/negative label ratio, filtering count or threshold is shown.
Different dashed colors are semantically close when printed in grayscale.
figures.reusable_pattern: Show structured supervision as difference graph → connected component → ordered label, with a visible terminal token and a place to report filtering counts.

figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Figure 5: Search curves for L2Seg on three backbone solvers on large capacity CVRP2k (upper) and CVRP5k (lower). L2Seg achieves up to 7x speedups.

color.semantic_mapping: Green, blue and mustard identify LKH-3, LNS and L2D; dashed/marker backbone lines versus solid augmented lines identify SYN; red guides and labels identify time-to-quality comparisons.

encodings.text: speedup labels and red time-to-quality guides

figures.data_and_statistics: Average objective-versus-time traces are shown for 100 large-capacity CVRP test instances at 2k and 5k. The upper panel annotates approximately 6.8x, 7.4x and 2.1x and the lower panel approximately 5.7x, 4.1x and 2.0x time-to-quality comparisons. No error bar, band, repeat count or quality threshold definition is visible.
figures.evidence_relation: The curves extend Table 1’s endpoint Obj/Gain/Time comparison into a dynamic search process. Red guides support the speedup claim, while the exact endpoints and time limits remain in Table 1 and Table 9.
design_strengths: Both problem scales share axes and a stable six-series color/line grammar.
Reference guides turn a static objective difference into a time-to-quality comparison.
Backbone identity and SYN augmentation are redundantly encoded by color and line style.
design_weaknesses: The legend and red guides become crowded in a narrow column.
The caption does not define averaging, the quality threshold or the speedup denominator.
No variability is shown for the average traces.
figures.reusable_pattern: For an iterative solver, pair an objective–time curve with same-quality reference guides and retain the same backbone colors across scales.

figures.label: Figure 6

caption.text: Figure 6: Illustration of L2Seg model behaviors.

color.semantic_mapping: Panel titles identify Ground Truth/SYN/NAR/AR; red dashed edges identify predicted unstable edges and route/node colors show the shared example.

encodings.x: none; panels are ordered by model behavior
encodings.y: none; identical route layout is repeated across panels
encodings.color: ground-truth/predicted unstable-edge roles and method panels
encodings.line: route lines versus red predicted-edge dashes

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual route overlay only. The four panels reuse one route example; there are no sample counts, edge-level probabilities, aggregate metrics or uncertainty displays.
figures.evidence_relation: The visual is the qualitative counterpart of Table 4’s Recall/TNR/Obj trade-off. It explains the NAR over-prediction and AR region-miss described in the main text, while Figure 12 provides a concrete appendix case.
design_strengths: A fixed route background isolates changes in the predicted overlay.
Four panels allow rapid comparison of the complementary failure modes.
The small legend gives a direct red-dash key.
design_weaknesses: The title-only caption does not explain the red dashed encoding or the panel conclusions.
The small panel size makes predicted versus true edges difficult to inspect.
The conceptual example cannot establish population-level behavior.
figures.reusable_pattern: Keep the route base fixed and change only the prediction overlay; write the over-predict and miss directions directly in the caption.

figures.label: Figure 7

caption.text: Figure 7: Statistic values of Size (reduced/original ratio), Recall, and TNR across three L2Seg-SYN configurations.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue/orange/green bars encode Size/Recall/TNR and a red objective line uses the secondary y-axis; configuration labels encode η and nKMEANS.

encodings.x: three categorical configurations: conservative, moderate and aggressive reduction
encodings.y: left axis for Size/Recall/TNR and right axis for Objective
encodings.color: Size, Recall, TNR bars and red Objective line
encodings.shape: bar groups and circular objective markers
encodings.text: η, nKMEANS, axis labels and legends

figures.data_and_statistics: The chart compares three SYN settings: conservative (η=0.9,nKMEANS=2), moderate (η=0.6,nKMEANS=3) and aggressive (η=0.3,nKMEANS=10). Rendered estimates are Size about 0.25/0.46/0.75 and objective about 47.0/43.3/46.1; the PDF does not print every bar value or any repeat/uncertainty statistic.
figures.evidence_relation: The configuration trade-off links Table 3/4’s performance to the reduction mechanism: too little or too much reduction harms objective, while the moderate setting balances TNR and Recall. Figure 11 studies the two knobs separately and Table 15 reports the resulting overhead.
design_strengths: One categorical axis aligns compression, prediction quality and task objective.
The red secondary-axis line makes the non-monotone trade-off visible.
The configuration labels expose the two control parameters.
design_weaknesses: The unlabelled dual y-axis increases directional ambiguity.
Long configuration labels and two legends are dense in the right column.
No numeric bar labels, repeats or uncertainty are provided.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a shared configuration axis for reduction, prediction quality and objective, but pair the dual-axis view with an exact value table and explicit axis units.

figures.label: Figure 8

caption.text: Figure 8: Spatial distribution of unstable edges (dashed red lines) across optimization iterations using LKH-3 solver. Results are presented for three randomly selected CVRP1k instances at iteatvie search steps 1 and 5. While many edges remain unchanged across iterations, unstable edges predominantly emerge within the interiors of routes. In contrast, edges located at route boundaries exhibit higher stability throughout the iterative optimization process.

color.semantic_mapping: Red dashed edges indicate unstable edges and black/gray lines indicate the route; row and column labels identify iteration and random instance.

encodings.color: unstable red edges versus stable black/gray route
encodings.line: route edges versus dashed unstable edges
encodings.facet: three random instances by two optimization steps

figures.data_and_statistics: Six route panels show three randomly selected CVRP1k instances at LKH-3 steps 1 and 5. This is a qualitative sample with no whole-dataset percentage, denominator, repeat distribution or uncertainty statistic; the caption states the interior-versus-boundary pattern.
figures.evidence_relation: The spatial example refines Figure 1’s aggregate decline into a location claim. It motivates segment formation in Figure 2/9 and is quantified across rounds by Table 14.
design_strengths: Shared coordinate ranges make the step-1 versus step-5 comparison direct.
The caption states sampling, color key and the interior/boundary finding.
The six-panel layout shows the pattern in multiple instances.
design_weaknesses: A three-instance sample cannot replace a population summary.
Red and black dashed/solid edges overlap visually at small size and in grayscale.
No edge counts or per-panel metric labels are shown.
figures.reusable_pattern: Repeat a common coordinate frame across optimization rounds and instances, then report overlap statistics in a companion table.

figures.label: Figure 9

caption.text: Figure 9: Illustration of our FSTA applied to one CVRP instance. Each FSTA step corresponds to the descriptions in Appendix B.1.4. Red dashed lines: unstable edges; blue dashed lines: re-optimized edges. Note that the subproblem (d) contains substantially fewer nodes than the original instance (a).

color.semantic_mapping: Red dashed edges are unstable, blue dashed edges are re-optimized, and black/gray lines are route structure; panel letters encode the FSTA stage.

encodings.color: unstable, re-optimized and unchanged route edges
encodings.line: red/blue dashed overlays and route connectors
encodings.facet: original, detection, partition, aggregation, re-optimization and recovery

figures.data_and_statistics: One CVRP instance is followed through six FSTA stages. Panel (d) visibly contains fewer nodes than (a); no aggregate sample size, objective or uncertainty is encoded.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 9 instantiates Figure 2’s abstract loop and the implementation in Algorithm 1. It connects the reduction mechanism to Table 7’s variant interface and the quality/time results in Tables 1 and 15.
design_strengths: The same instance and coordinate frame persist through all six stages.
The caption defines both dashed-edge roles and points to the detailed algorithm.
The reduction is visually concrete rather than only asserted in text.
design_weaknesses: A single instance does not establish average reduction or quality.
Dense routes and node labels are hard to inspect at page scale.
The mapping from partitioned segments to hypernodes needs the surrounding text.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use one traceable instance for detection → partition → aggregation → re-optimization → recovery, preserving coordinates and adding one overlay per stage.

figures.label: Figure 10

caption.text: Figure 10: This illustration demonstrates the temporal dynamics of the aggregated segment. The left panel shows the time function characterized by a piecewise linear structure: initially decreasing with slope -1, then transitioning to a constant value corresponding to the aggregated left time window boundary. The right panel presents two distinct scenarios that characterize the relationship between the aggregated left time window (t̄lm) and the individual non-aggregated left time windows (tlm).

color.semantic_mapping: Pink case boxes, green nodes/boundaries and black piecewise line/text encode the two VRPTW time-window cases.

encodings.x: arrival time at node x_m in the left panel and time-window positions in case panels
encodings.y: total time spent on segment S_m,k and window-boundary geometry
encodings.color: case boxes, nodes and boundary roles
encodings.line: piecewise function and dashed time-window guides

figures.data_and_statistics: Deterministic illustration of the VRPTW aggregation rule. The left function has slope -1 followed by a constant segment; the right cases compare aggregated and individual left windows. No data sample, estimate or uncertainty is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: The figure explains the VRPTW conditions implemented in Table 7 and the proof in Appendix B.2. Its interface is used by the VRPTW rows in Table 2; it is not an empirical curve.
design_strengths: The slope change gives an intuitive geometric reading of the timing constraint.
The two right-hand cases make the boundary condition explicit.
Caption names both panels and preserves the mathematical relationship.
design_weaknesses: Small equations and case annotations require high zoom.
No concrete time unit or instance is supplied.
The meaning of some boundary guides is deferred to the appendix text.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a piecewise function with two boundary cases, retaining the same variable names in the interface table and proof.

figures.label: Figure 11

caption.text: Figure 11: Analysis of key hyperparameters: (a) number of clusters nMEANS, and (b) balancing factor η.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue line and circular markers encode the objective sweep; x labels identify n_KMEANS and η values.

encodings.x: discrete n_KMEANS values 2, 3, 5, 10 and η values 0.3, 0.6, 0.9

figures.data_and_statistics: Two one-factor objective sweeps support the default n_KMEANS=3 and η=0.6 choices. Values are point estimates without repeat count, error bars or printed data labels; the caption’s `nMEANS` spelling is retained exactly as rendered while the paper’s parameter table uses n_KMEANS.
figures.evidence_relation: The appendix makes the defaults used in Table 9 visible and complements Figure 7’s three combined configurations. It is a sensitivity support, not a full hyperparameter search or uncertainty analysis.
design_strengths: Both sweeps use the same compact line grammar and objective axis.
Default candidates are visible near the best part of each curve.
A single-color encoding is relatively safe in grayscale.
design_weaknesses: The caption contains the nMEANS/n_KMEANS inconsistency.
No exact values, repetitions or variability are provided.
Small panels and no legend make the plotted metric depend on the axis label.
figures.reusable_pattern: Show one-factor sweeps with shared y semantics and explicitly mark the selected default; keep parameter spelling consistent across caption and table.

figures.label: Figure 12

caption.text: Figure 12: Prediction comparison of L2Seg-SYN, L2Seg-NAR, and L2Seg-AR on two adjacent routes from a small-capacity CVRP1k solution. Red dashed lines indicate predicted unstable edges. L2Seg-SYN provides the most reasonable predictions, while L2Seg-NAR over-predicts unstable edges and L2Seg-AR fails to identify unstable regions.

color.semantic_mapping: Panel labels identify SYN/NAR/AR; red dashed edges identify predictions and black/gray edges retain the route base.

encodings.color: predicted red edges versus route lines
encodings.line: route connectors versus red dashed prediction overlays
encodings.text: model panel labels and caption key

figures.data_and_statistics: A single small-capacity CVRP1k solution contributes two adjacent route examples. The comparison is qualitative: no edge-level counts, probabilities, sample denominator or uncertainty is displayed.
figures.evidence_relation: The case study makes Table 4’s Recall/TNR trade-off and Figure 6’s conceptual behavior visible on a fixed local route. It complements Table 14’s aggregate edge overlap rather than replacing it.
design_strengths: A fixed two-route base isolates the model-specific prediction overlay.
The caption states the direction of all three behavior differences.
Three panels are compact enough for a direct qualitative comparison.
design_weaknesses: One case cannot quantify over-prediction or missed regions.
No ground-truth overlay or numeric edge count is shown.
Red/black distinction weakens in grayscale and at small size.
figures.reusable_pattern: Hold adjacent routes fixed and compare only the prediction overlay, then pair the case with a quantitative Recall/TNR or overlap table.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1: Performance comparisons of our proposed L2Seg-NAR, L2Seg-AR, and L2Seg-SYN when accelerating three backbone solvers, LKH-3, LNS, and L2D, on the large-capacity CVRP instances. We report the objective value, improvement gain (%), and the time. The gains (the higher the better) are w.r.t. the performance of each backbone solver. Time limits were set to be 150s for CVRP2k and 240s for CVRP5k, respectively.

tables.uncertainty: No error bars, intervals, standard deviations or failure counts are shown; Gain is a point improvement relative to each corresponding backbone.
tables.data_and_statistics: Twelve rows cover LKH-3, LNS and L2D plus NAR, AR and SYN variants. The two scale blocks use Obj/Gain/Time. Baseline values are LKH-3 45.24/65.34, LNS 44.92/64.69 and L2D 43.69/64.21 for CVRP2k/5k; SYN rows reach 43.92/64.12, 43.42/63.94 and 43.35/63.89 respectively, with exact PDF values for all NAR/AR rows.
tables.evidence_relation: The main endpoint comparison tests whether the FSTA/L2Seg interface in Figures 2–4 improves each backbone under the stated limits. Figure 5 supplies the dynamic time-to-quality view.
design_strengths: Backbone row groups make within-solver comparisons fair.
Obj, Gain and Time appear as a stable three-column bundle.
Caption defines gain direction and both scale limits.
design_weaknesses: Seven columns in a narrow column make seconds and percentages dense.
The table header does not itself show Obj/Gain/Time directions as clearly as the caption.
No trial variability is reported.
tables.reusable_pattern: Nest learned variants under each backbone and report objective, relative gain and time together.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2: Performance comparisons of our L2Seg-SYN-L2D against baselines on benchmark CVRP and VRPTW instances. The gap % (lower the better) is w.r.t. the performance of HGS.

tables.uncertainty: Point estimates only. No standard deviation, interval, repeat count or failure count is shown; `-` denotes an unavailable method/scale result in the PDF.
tables.data_and_statistics: The table has 19 logical columns: Methods plus Obj/Gap/Time for CVRP1k, CVRP2k, CVRP5k and the corresponding three VRPTW scales. L2Seg-SYN-L2D is 41.23/0.07%/2.5m, 56.05/-2.01%/4.1m and 121.87/-3.55%/5.1m on CVRP; it is 87.25/-3.43%/2m, 163.74/-5.60%/4m and 333.4/-3.14%/10m on VRPTW. The PDF also retains all listed classic and neural baselines.
tables.evidence_relation: This broad comparison extends Table 1 from within-backbone augmentation to classic and neural baselines across CVRP and VRPTW. It relies on Figure 2’s method interface and Table 9’s scale-specific limits; Table 12 tests distribution variants.
design_strengths: CVRP and VRPTW reuse the same Obj/Gap/Time grammar.
The HGS gap reference is stated in the caption.
Missing baseline values remain explicit rather than silently imputed.
design_weaknesses: Nineteen logical columns and mixed time units are difficult to scan.
Negative gaps and unavailable dashes need the surrounding text for interpretation.
No variability is shown despite many cross-method comparisons.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use task-family column blocks with identical quality/reference/time triples, and write one unit and missing-value rule in the caption.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3: Performance of L2Seg-SYN v.s. Random FSTA to accelerate LNS on CVRP instances.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty or repeat information is shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: CVRP2k Obj values are LNS 44.92, Random FSTA 40% 46.24, Random FSTA 60% 46.89, SYN without Enhanced Features 43.65 and full SYN 43.42. CVRP5k values are 64.69, 66.72, 65.92, 64.22 and 63.94. Obj is lower-is-better.
tables.evidence_relation: The random-FSTA and feature-removal counterfactuals test the stable-edge and enhanced-feature mechanisms behind Figure 2 and Figure 7. Full SYN is the endpoint used in Table 1.
design_strengths: The two-row table maps directly to the two target scales.
Random and no-feature counterfactuals sit beside the full method.
The best objective is visually easy to locate.
design_weaknesses: The caption does not define 40%/60%, Enhanced Features or objective direction.
The `v.s.` abbreviation is informal.
There is no trial variability or time budget.
tables.reusable_pattern: Put random segmentation and feature removal beside the complete method so the mechanism claim is tested with minimal columns.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4: Model prediction analysis of L2Seg-LNS on CVRP2k.

tables.uncertainty: Point estimates only; no edge-label denominator, repeat count, interval or standard deviation is printed.
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows are L2Seg-SYN 89.02% Recall, 61.24% TNR, 43.42 Obj; L2Seg-NAR 91.46%, 51.79%, 44.02; and L2Seg-AR 74.39%, 54.07%, 44.12. Recall/TNR are higher-is-better and Obj is lower-is-better.
tables.evidence_relation: Recall and TNR explain the behavior contrast in Figure 6 and the balanced moderate configuration in Figure 7. Obj links the local edge prediction measures back to the LNS endpoint in Table 1.
design_strengths: Prediction metrics and task objective are adjacent.
The three decoder variants have a consistent row order with Figures 2, 3 and 6.
Arrow directions make the intended optimization direction visible.
design_weaknesses: Caption omits metric definitions, denominators and time setting.
Bold selection is not explained in the caption.
Point estimates do not reveal label variability.
tables.reusable_pattern: Report local classification quality beside the final routing objective so high Recall is not mistaken for overall success.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: Table 5: Label similarity across different solvers

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty or per-seed spread is shown, although the text says each solver used 10 seeds.
tables.data_and_statistics: The single Label Similarity row reports HGS 78.3%, LKH-3 at 1000 local-search steps 85.1%, and LKH-3 at 3000 steps 100% as the default reference. Similarity is overlapping stable edges; the text defines 60s HGS and a 10-seed procedure.
tables.evidence_relation: The table tests whether stability labels are inherent to the problem or solver-dependent. It supports the shared-structure premise behind Figure 1 and FSTA, while the 3000-step LKH-3 column acts as the ground truth reference.
design_strengths: One short row gives the mechanism result without unnecessary decoration.
Solver identities and step counts are explicit in the header.
The reference 100% provides an interpretable anchor.
design_weaknesses: The caption does not define similarity or the reference construction.
Ten-seed information is outside the table.
A single percentage row cannot show between-seed variability.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a reference solver column and explicit overlap percentages to separate problem-inherent stability from solver-specific labels.

tables.label: Table 6

caption.text: Table 6: Oracle Performance on CVRP2k: Time to Reach L2Seg-SYN-LNS Solution Quality

tables.uncertainty: Oracle look-ahead computation is excluded by the appendix text; no repeats, intervals or oracle-generation overhead are reported.
tables.data_and_statistics: Obj row is 56.02, 56.01, 56.02, 56.04 and 56.08 for perfect, 95%, 90%, 70% Recall/TNR oracle conditions and the L2Seg-SYN-LNS reference. Time row is 39s, 62s, 119s, 324s and 241s.
tables.evidence_relation: The sensitivity table connects Table 4 prediction quality to time needed to reach the learned-model solution quality. Because look-ahead cost is excluded, it is a mechanism/oracle analysis rather than a fair end-to-end speed comparison.
design_strengths: Recall/TNR degradation is ordered as a clear sensitivity axis.
Obj and Time are compactly paired.
The reference column makes the learned system’s position visible.
design_weaknesses: Long oracle headers are hard to scan.
The caption does not state the excluded look-ahead cost or Obj direction.
No variability or computational cost decomposition is shown.
tables.reusable_pattern: Arrange perfect-to-imperfect oracle conditions beside the learned reference and explicitly flag any oracle cost excluded from timing.

tables.label: Table 7

caption.text: Table 7: Implementation specifications of FSTA hypernode aggregation for CVRP, VRPTW, VRPB variants. Refer to Equation 3 for the definitions of s̄j, t̄lj and t̄rj.

tables.uncertainty: Deterministic implementation rules; no experimental sample, estimator or uncertainty applies.
tables.data_and_statistics: Four problem-family groups define Type, Condition, Attribute, Aggregation and Additional Constraints/Settings. CVRP uses two hypernodes and averaged demand; VRPTW branches on t̄lj≤t̄rj versus t̄lj>t̄rj with service/time-window transformations; VRPB preserves customer type; 1-VRPPD uses three hypernodes and Dmin/Dmax/Dk demand splits. The PDF’s body includes 1-VRPPD even though the caption names only the first three variants.
tables.evidence_relation: The table makes the hypernode interface in Figures 2 and 9 implementable, supplies the VRPTW cases illustrated in Figure 10, and anchors the cross-problem results in Table 2.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 establishes that most iterative edges are stable, Figures 2–4 expose FSTA and L2Seg interfaces, Table 1/Table 2 and Figure 5 report quality and time, Table 3/Table 4 and Figures 6–7 explain ablations, and Figures 8–12 plus Tables 6–16 provide spatial, variant, reproduction, robustness and cost boundaries. The sequence moves from local edge mechanism to end-to-end VRP solver outcomes.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Every object uses a stable Figure/Table n: prefix. Architecture and process captions often provide setup and encoding keys, while result captions add comparison references or time limits. Figure 6 and many appendix tables use title-only or short captions, leaving units, directions and aggregation to the surrounding text. PDF spellings `iteatvie` in Figure 8 and `nMEANS` in Figure 11 are preserved as rendered facts.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Main result tables reuse method/backbone × scale × Obj/Gain/Time or Obj/Gap/Time groupings. Appendix tables use problem-family, parameter, metric, round and scale row/column groups. Booktabs-like horizontal rules and local bolding are common, but units and direction markers are not consistently carried into the header.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figures 2–4 and Tables 8–10 define the FSTA, feature and network interfaces; Tables 1–2 and Figure 5 measure solver quality and speed; Table 3–4 and Figures 6–7/11/12 connect feature, Recall/TNR, configuration and behavior ablations back to the endpoint. Tables 13–15 test variability, convergence and overhead.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–5 carry motivation, method and headline comparisons. Appendix Figures 8–10 and Table 6–7 explain stability, FSTA variants and VRPTW constraints; Tables 8–10 give inputs and constants; Figures 11–12 and Tables 11–16 cover hyperparameters, realistic distributions, repeated trials, convergence and cost.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Page text and tables share Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern objects, but imported diagrams and raster panels add Arial/Aptos/CambriaMath-like or untraceable fonts. Figure/table captions are stable, while 6–8 pt labels in dense architecture, route and multi-column objects are the main readability limit.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Red dashed unstable edges and blue dashed re-optimized edges are stable across route figures. SYN/NAR/AR colors recur in method and result figures, while tables are mostly black/white with bold emphasis. The pastel method palette and saturated quantitative palette form related but not identical sub-systems, so labels and line styles are necessary redundancy.

most_reusable_patterns: Use one iteration-level stability curve to motivate the optimization reduction, then show a single-instance six-step FSTA walkthrough.
Keep a stable Obj/Gain/Time or Obj/Gap/Time schema across backbone, scale and method comparisons, with objective–time curves as the dynamic supplement.
Hold a route base fixed while changing NAR, AR and SYN overlays, then pair the qualitative behavior with Recall/TNR/Obj metrics.
Separate variant interfaces, reproduction constants, repeated-trial stability and online/offline cost into appendix objects that point back to the headline chain.
failure_patterns: A visible band in Figure 1 has no statistical definition and must not be read as a conventional interval.
Figure 5 speedup annotations lack a stated quality threshold and averaging rule.
Short captions omit directions, units or definitions in Figure 6, Figure 7 and Tables 3–6 and 14–16.
Dual axes, long multi-level headers, 6–7 pt labels and color dependence reduce grayscale and small-size readability; most objects lack repeat variability except Table 13.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses a stable-edge motivation → FSTA/SYN interface → dynamic search gain → prediction-behavior ablation → appendix boundary sequence to show how local route structure becomes measurable VRP acceleration, but more self-contained captions, uniform units and explicit uncertainty definitions would lower interpretation cost.
